newsitem.title: USA: Northland ends talks on Atoka purchase.
newsitem.headline: Northland ends talks on Atoka purchase.

text.p: Northland Cranberries Inc and Atoka Cranberries Inc have terminated discussions on Northland's proposed acquisition of Atoka, Northland said Thursday.
After extensive discussions and due diligence, Northland and Atoka agreed to end negotiations because of philosophical differences regarding Atoka's future operations and expansion, Northland said.
It also cited "certain structural aspects of the transaction which...would likely impact the synergies desired from the proposed acquisition."

Northland said the termination of the negotiations was not expected to have any material impact on anticipated earnings or results of operations for its fiscal years ending August 31, 1997, and August 31, 1998.
In May, Northland said it had entered into an agreement to acquire Atoka, the owner of North America's largest single-site cranberry bog, for $28.5 million.
At the time, Northland said the transaction was to be payable $13 million in cash and the remainder in Northland convertible notes.
Northland is the world's largest cranberry grower and makes 100 percent blended cranberry juice products.
